summary.intent: Execute a multi-lane background pass to fix four CipherBox issues (#2016, #2021, #1956, #2017) from a handoff document, driving three parallel agent lanes through implementation, nested reviews, CI, CodeRabbit, and merge, then follow up with ADR/blueprint documentation updates for the durable-shape and behavioral changes introduced.
summary.outcome: All three PRs (2059, 2060, 2063) merged and their four issues closed, with main green (24 suites, 2800 tests) after each merge; cleaned up 37 stale placeholder branches; wrote two ADR PRs (2081 ADR 0054, 2082 ADR 0055) with CI green, then revised both per the repo's ADR quality-gate rules (folding a weak D3 into D2, moving accepted residuals into Consequences) and pushed the fixes.

repo: CipherBox repo enforces an ADR quality-gate rubric with three checks per decision (not clear without context, real trade-off, hard to reverse) and a rule that Residuals should hold only open owner questions, not accepted residuals (those go in Consequences as one-liners)
ADR index table in the repo is prettier-formatted and reflows/rewraps when a new row is added, causing incidental diff noise

CodeRabbit full-review requests are slot-gated (one at a time) and require waiting for a floor time before posting; the request script needs to run detached since it can exceed the 10-minute Bash tool timeout

Nested review agents (simplify: reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude, security, crypto-privacy, code-review) are launched by lane agents themselves and their results route back to the orchestrating session, requiring manual forwarding to the lane

Squash-merged PRs still leave placeholder branches in removed agent worktrees; branch content should be verified against main before deletion (one instance matched a squash-merge of a different PR number)
AGENTS.md comment rules forbid narrating code behavior or restating invariants in comments; this recurred as a code-review finding across multiple PRs

code.finding: run_past_deadline hand-wrote a poll_fn race duplicating the existing `within` combinator in record_plane.rs:153; flagged by three independent reviewers (reuse, simplification, altitude) across lane B's PR
staleness_now wrote `reported` on every read causing side effects in reads and duplicating classify() logic present in report_rung; fixed via SyncStatus::observe

refuse_below_cut_floor duplicated an existing stage-2 cut-floor check (cipherbox_core::seal::refuse_stale_cut_epoch) already used by the gate; ended up copied in three places (drain, and two rotation.rs sites) with two different rejection verdicts before being consolidated

retire ledger format was extended to carry whole root blocks tagged by trailing byte length, breaking the ledger's 'small relative to CID set' design goal and requiring a versioned entry grammar (0x02 prefix) in the eventual fix

live_owing_record's Edit rule compared only head CID vs base, allowing a dropped version to resurface if a later record ties/loses race at the same sequence; fixed by introducing an acknowledged-sequence mark (cbx/ra/<node> key) that publishes must sign above

workflow: Running independent lanes as background agents with nested sub-review agents lets the orchestrator do parallel diff review and CodeRabbit slot management while lanes work, but requires diligent state-checking (worktree, PR existence) each time a lane agent stops silently between phases
Detached/monitor-based waiting (Monitor tool with 'legs') is used to survive tool timeouts and Opus session-limit resets without blocking the main thread
Session/rate limits (Opus 'hits session limit') can kill a lane mid-task; recovery requires re-sending resume instructions after the reset time and verifying the lane's worktree/commit state first

friction: Lane C stopped twice mid-sequence (after simplify pass, then after security review) without a final report, requiring manual resume via SendMessage each time
Lane A hit the Opus session rate limit and died mid-task with 'resets 8:20pm (Europe/Berlin)', losing ~3 hours of wall-clock time until it could be resumed
Background Bash tool has a 10-minute cap that couldn't cover an 11-minute CodeRabbit slot wait, requiring a detached-process workaround
CodeRabbit review requests are serialized to one slot at a time across all three PRs, adding significant sequential wait time to an otherwise parallel workflow
One post-merge Monitor task ('Request the CodeRabbit full review on PR 2063') did not survive a session restart and had to be re-checked/re-armed
open_items: ADR 0053 PR touches the same ADR index table as 2081/2082, so the second of those merged will need a one-line rebase
Follow-up issue #2065 filed for the case where a dropped version's staged root block is already gone before rows can be journaled (charge-time journal proposed as fix)
Drain still signs a scope root without taking the write-epoch lease (documented rationale in PR 2063 body, tied to ADR 0041 E2) — left as accepted design, not fixed

Retire-ledger accepted residuals left undone: mark key persists after rotation (one leftover key per node), mark key metadata reveals node id similarly to tombstone keys, and a double-failed mark write before a dead-lettered rebase can lose the mark
T3 worktree on staging-soak branch (zero commits ahead of main) intentionally left alone since another thread owns it
